attributes.probed_form:
SIX LITERAL FORMS ON TWO AXES. Forms 1-4 are carried forward VERBATIM from the superseded attempt.ct-movieplayer-named-ctor-home-vs-save-two-sided.20260901.v1 so this record is the complete trail; forms 5-6 are new this run.

THE RESIDUAL, read aligned first (`python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/movie/movieplayer __ct__11MoviePlayerFv --diff --raw`, whole 25-instruction body). Exactly one instruction sits in a different place; every other word is `=`:
  T  10: stwu r1,-24(r1)     O  10: stwu r1,-24(r1)
  T  14: stw r31,20(r1)      O  14: stw r3,8(r1)
  T  18: stw r3,8(r1)        O  18: lis r3,@ha __vt__11MoviePlayer
  T  1c: lis r3,@ha          O  1c: addi r0,r3,@lo
  T  20: addi r0,r3,@lo      O  20: stw r31,20(r1)
  T  24: lwz r31,8(r1)       O  24: lwz r31,8(r1)
TWO MECHANISMS, re-verified this run: (A) the target saves r31 in the prologue proper, right after the stwu; ours SINKS the save to immediately before r31's first definition (`lwz r31,8(r1)` at +0x24). (B) the target homes `this` at 8(r1) and reloads it into r31, reusing r3 as scratch for the second vtable address. Ours already has (B) exactly right -- it is why the retained form scores real 2 at 25/25.

FORM 1 (carried forward): a real `MoviePlayer::MoviePlayer()` member with `self = (u32*)this`. FIXES (A) EXACTLY -- save lands at +0x14 -- and never produces (B). real 7, 24 insns vs the target's 25.
FORM 2: the same member form with member-array `words[]` access. real 7, NEUTRAL against form 1 -- two identical results kill the natural-access axis.
FORM 3: a `volatile` home local inside the member form. real 11; adds a store and forces stmw.
FORM 4: both vtable addresses hoisted into temps so both are live as in the target. real 17, multiset 3t, still 24 insns.
FORM 5 (NEW): `#pragma scheduling off` immediately above the retained free-function form, body untouched:
    #pragma scheduling off
    u32* __ct__11MoviePlayerFv(u32* volatile p) {
RESULT: REGRESSED, real 2 -> 12, insns still T25/O25, multiset 0t. RAW WORDS 4 -> 14 (+10); DECODE went REGFIELD-ONLY 0 / IMMEDIATE 1 / OPCODE 3 to REGFIELD-ONLY 0 / IMMEDIATE 0 / OPCODE 14. AND THE SAVE DID NOT MOVE: the `--ops` cluster reads `replace T[9:10]@24-28=['lwz'] O[8:11]@20-2c=['stw','lis','addi']`, i.e. `stw r31,20(r1)` is still at +0x20. DECISIVE FINDING: the sunk save is NOT a list-scheduler decision. Disabling the scheduler leaves it exactly where it was and rearranges eight other words away from the target.
FORM 6 (NEW): `#pragma optimization_level 3` immediately above the same unchanged body:
    #pragma optimization_level 3
    u32* __ct__11MoviePlayerFv(u32* volatile p) {
RESULT: NEUTRAL, real 2, insns T25/O25, RAW WORDS 4, DECODE REGFIELD-ONLY 0 / IMMEDIATE 1 / OPCODE 3 -- the baseline residual, unchanged in every field. The save is still at +0x20, confirmed by re-reading the object: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/movie/movieplayer __ct__11MoviePlayerFv 0x10:0x28 --diff --raw` reproduces the six rows quoted above verbatim. The save placement is not an optimisation-LEVEL decision either.

THE STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT THE SIX FORMS ADD UP TO, and the reason this is an exhaustion rather than a sixth dead end. (B) is supplied in our tree by exactly one construct: the `volatile` qualifier on the parameter, which obliges MWCC to store the incoming r3 to its home slot and re-read it. (A) is supplied, measurably (form 1), by exactly one construct: writing the function as a real C++ constructor, whose EH-bearing prologue emits the callee-saved save before the parameter home instead of sinking it. A C++ constructor's `this` is IMPLICIT and cannot carry a volatile qualifier, so the lever that supplies (B) is not expressible in the form that supplies (A). The two mechanisms are mutually exclusive at the level of C++ declaration syntax, not merely unobtained. Forms 5 and 6 close the remaining direction -- getting (A) from the free-function side by changing the compiler's behaviour rather than the source -- and both fail while holding the body exactly constant.
